title: Tiered fallback prioritizer and scaling-fingerprint investigation for dedicated pool shortfall
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Summary: During a customer-facing throughput shortfall on a dedicated GPU pool we observed a ~35% drop in tail throughput over a 40m window. This ticket tracks the immediate containment technique (tiered fallback prioritizer + middle-tier rate limiter), the post-incident forensic investigation (scaling fingerprinting), and the follow-up roadmap to prevent recurrence. Goal: minimize customer-visible SLA violations and produce concrete remediation steps for autoscaler, routing, and observability. This is not a postmortem doc — it contains live-run notes, hypotheses, quick mitigations, and explicit action items assigned for a longer-term fix.
summary: Contain capacity shortfall with tenant-prioritized degradation, fingerprint the regression signal to root-cause autoscaler/serving mismatch, and deliver hardening to prevent recurrence.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-28 09:12 UTC: Alert - dedicated-pool-nyc-2 tail latency and queue-length exceed SLA thresholds.
2026-02-28 09:15 UTC: Grafana dashboard shows KV cache miss ratio spike and a sudden increase in average sequence length from a subset of tenants.
2026-02-28 09:22 UTC: Autoscaler did not add nodes due to low aggregate CPU signal; queueing rose and p50 latency remained within target leading to slow response to tail degradation.
2026-02-28 09:30 UTC: Deployed emergency middle-tier rate limiter and tenant-priority fallback which restored tail throughput for high-priority tenants within 6 minutes.
2026-02-28 10:00 UTC: Incident declared resolved for customer-impacting requests; full forensic investigation initiated.
hypotheses: Autoscaler signal mismatch: scaler uses aggregated CPU and avg request rate and misses localized KV-cache pressure caused by a few high-seqlen tenants.
Model variant heterogeneity: a recent model rollout increased memory pressure on a subpool causing scheduling jitter and eviction churn.
Workload skew: nonuniform tenant distribution created bursty tails that didn't trigger scaling because P50 stayed stable.
Regression in kernel scheduling introduced variability under high KV-cache miss-rate leading to throughput collapse at tail.
mitigations_applied: Activated 'tiered fallback prioritizer' — graceful degradation policy that classifies requests into priority tiers (SLA-critical, standard, best-effort) and preemptively reassigns lower-priority requests to best-effort variants.
Deployed middle-tier token-bucket rate limiter per tenant with emergency quota thresholds to arrest queue growth while preserving high-priority traffic.
Enabled conservative autoscaler override: temporary scale-up of dedicated-pool-nyc-2 by 20% for 30 minutes to buy time for investigation.
Routed shadow-traffic of newly onboarded model variant to isolated canary to check memory/KV behavior.
telemetry_actions: Added a 'scaling-fingerprint' event that captures: per-tenant seqlen distribution, KV cache miss ratio, request concurrency histogram, and node-level eviction rates at 10s granularity.
Instrumented autoscaler to report the exact input signals used for decisions (cpu_avg, tokens_per_minute, queue_depth_percentile) to a dedicated Grafana panel.
Created a short-lived 'incident' retention stream in long-term storage for correlated traces and payload hashes for 7 days.
forensics_findings: Scaling trigger delta: autoscaler threshold logic used a 5m rolling avg which smoothed out the initial burst from 09:14-09:18, preventing scale-up.
KV cache correlation: tenants responsible for the burst had a 4x increase in KV cache miss ratio coincident with longer sequences, increasing per-request latency and reducing effective throughput.
Model rollout correlation: a canary model ramp at 08:50 increased memory fragmentation on a subset of nodes, compounding eviction churn under burst.
tradeoffs_considered: Aggressive autoscale: lowering averaging window would react faster but may cause oscillation and overspend under noisy traffic.
Preemptive tenant throttling: reduces observed tail but risks frustrating developer experience for lower-tier customers.
Pinned model variants: reduces heterogeneity and risk but limits quick rollout of optimizations.
decisions: Short-term: keep tiered fallback prioritizer and per-tenant rate limiter enabled for 2 weeks while monitoring impact on errors and customer complaints.
Autoscaler: change scale trigger to include a high-percentile queue_depth signal (p95 queue depth) in addition to cpu_avg; reduce smoothing window from 5m to 90s for queue-based triggers.
Observability: ship 'scaling-fingerprint' to prod and backfill last 48 hours for classifiers and RCA.
next_steps: ENG: implement autoscaler code change (add p95 queue depth signal + 90s smoothing) and run canary in staging — PR #13480
ENG: formalize 'tiered fallback' policy in routing layer and add opt-out flags for enterprise tenants — PR #13495
PM: contact top 10 affected tenants with incident summary and temporary mitigations; collect feedback on fallback UX
SRE/Oncall: update runbook with new detection thresholds and a quick checklist to enable tiered fallback and temporary scale overrides
Infra: schedule a targeted canary rollback test to reproduce memory fragmentation behavior under synthetic high-seq workloads.
